This is the description of the feature that I want to implement:

<pasted_content id="6ee9">
What happens after the admin turns the switch on
An existing user logs in, and they don’t have 2FA
Type their email and password
Severs checks two things: is the switch on, and does this user lack 2FA? If both are true, markes them as having to set up 2FA
A popup appears that they can’t close. Walks them through the 2FA set up.
When they finish, the use the app normally

A new user signs up with email and password:
Have to set up 2FA before creating their account

Nothing changes for:
users who already have 2FA
users who sign in with Google or another provider
everyone, if the switch is off
</pasted_content id="6ee9">

There is a design choice that has to be made for how the popup goes away once the user finishes setting up 2FA. But that will be addressed later. 

Am i correct in assuming that a change needs to be made in this file packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts

```text
/**
 * Authorize function for credentials provider
 * Extracted for testability
 */
export async function authorizeCredentials(
  credentials: Record<"email" | "password" | "totpCode" | "backupCode", string> | undefined
): Promise<User | null> {
  log.debug("CredentialsProvider:credentials:authorize", safeStringify({ credentials }));
  if (!credentials) {
    console.error(`For some reason credentials are missing`);
    throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError);
  }

  const userRepo = new UserRepository(prisma);
  const user = await userRepo.findByEmailAndIncludeProfilesAndPassword({
    email: credentials.email,
  });
  // Don't leak information about it being username or password that is invalid
  if (!user) {
    throw new Error(ErrorCode.IncorrectEmailPassword);
  }

  // Locked users cannot login
  if (user.locked) {
    throw new Error(ErrorCode.UserAccountLocked);
  }

  await checkRateLimitAndThrowError({
    identifier: hashEmail(user.email),
  });

  // Users without a password must use their identity provider (Google/SAML) to login
  if (!user.password?.hash) {
    throw new Error(ErrorCode.IncorrectEmailPassword);
  }

  // Always verify password for users who have one
  const isCorrectPassword = await verifyPassword(credentials.password, user.password.hash);
  if (!isCorrectPassword) {
    throw new Error(ErrorCode.IncorrectEmailPassword);
  }

  if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode) {
    if (!process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) {
      console.error("Missing encryption key; cannot proceed with backup code login.");
      throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError);
    }

    if (!user.backupCodes) throw new Error(ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes);

    const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY));

    // check if user-supplied code matches one
    const index = backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""));
    if (index === -1) throw new Error(ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode);

    // delete verified backup code and re-encrypt remaining
    backupCodes[index] = null;
    await prisma.user.update({
      where: {
        id: user.id,
      },
      data: {
        backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY),
      },
    });
  } else if (user.twoFactorEnabled) {
    if (!credentials.totpCode) {
      throw new Error(ErrorCode.SecondFactorRequired);
    }

    if (!user.twoFactorSecret) {
      console.error(`Two factor is enabled for user ${user.id} but they have no secret`);
      throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError);
    }

    if (!process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) {
      console.error(`"Missing encryption key; cannot proceed with two factor login."`);
      throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError);
    }

    const secret = symmetricDecrypt(user.twoFactorSecret, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY);
    if (secret.length !== 32) {
      console.error(
        `Two factor secret decryption failed. Expected key with length 32 but got ${secret.length}`
      );
      throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError);
    }

    const isValidToken = (await import("@calcom/lib/totp")).totpAuthenticatorCheck(
      credentials.totpCode,
      secret
    );
    if (!isValidToken) {
      throw new Error(ErrorCode.IncorrectTwoFactorCode);
    }
  }
  // Check if the user you are logging into has any active teams
  const hasActiveTeams = checkIfUserBelongsToActiveTeam(user);

  // authentication success- but does it meet the minimum password requirements?
  const validateRole = (role: UserPermissionRole) => {
    // User's role is not "ADMIN"
    if (role !== UserPermissionRole.ADMIN) return role;
    // User's identity provider is not "CAL"
    if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL) return role;

    if (process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E) {
      console.warn("E2E testing is enabled, skipping password and 2FA requirements for Admin");
      return role;
    }

    // User's password is valid and two-factor authentication is enabled
    if (isPasswordValid(credentials.password, false, true) && user.twoFactorEnabled) return role;
    // Code is running in a development environment
    if (isENVDev) return role;
    // By this point it is an ADMIN without valid security conditions
    return "INACTIVE_ADMIN";
  };

  const role = validateRole(user.role);
  const baseUser = AdapterUserPresenter.fromCalUser(user, role, hasActiveTeams);

  if (role === "INACTIVE_ADMIN") {
    const passwordValid = isPasswordValid(credentials.password, false, true);
    const has2FA = user.twoFactorEnabled;

    let reason: "both" | "password" | "2fa";

    if (!passwordValid && !has2FA) {
      reason = "both";
    } else if (!passwordValid) {
      reason = "password";
    } else {
      reason = "2fa";
    }

    return { ...baseUser, inactiveAdminReason: reason };
  }

  return baseUser;
}
```

Yes, that file needs changes, but only for the login half of the feature. The signup half and the popup are in other places.

## What changes in `next-auth-options.ts`

There's already a working example of this exact pattern in the file: `inactiveAdminReason`. It's how the server flags an admin with a weak password or no 2FA, and the flag reaches the UI (`AdminPasswordBanner`). You'd add a second flag, something like `requiresTwoFactorSetup`, and pass it through the same three places:

1. **`authorizeCredentials`** ([next-auth-options.ts:151](packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts#L151)). This is where the server checks "is the switch on, and does this user lack 2FA?" Put the check after the password and TOTP checks, around [line 243](packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts#L243). Only call `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide()` when `!user.twoFactorEnabled`, so users who already have 2FA don't trigger an extra feature-flag lookup.
2. **The `jwt` callback, credentials branch** ([line 548](packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts#L548)). Copy the flag onto the token, the same way `inactiveAdminReason: user.inactiveAdminReason` is copied at [line 562](packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts#L562).
3. **The `session` callback** ([line 765](packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts#L765)). Copy it from the token onto `session.user`, like [line 783](packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts#L783).

You'll also need to add the field to both the `User` and `JWT` types in [packages/types/next-auth.d.ts](packages/types/next-auth.d.ts#L45), where `inactiveAdminReason` is declared at lines 45 and 62.

## What doesn't need to change in that file

- **Google and other providers:** `authorizeCredentials` only runs for email and password logins. Google, SAML and other OAuth sign-ins go through the `signIn` callback and the OAuth branch of `jwt`. If you leave those alone, those users are excluded automatically.
- **Switch off, or user already has 2FA:** the check returns early in both cases, so nothing changes for them.

## Where the rest of the work goes

- **New user signup:** [apps/web/app/api/auth/signup/handlers/](apps/web/app/api/auth/signup/handlers/). There are two handlers, `calcomSignupHandler.ts` and `selfHostedHandler.ts`, plus the signup form UI. This half is harder, because setting up 2FA currently assumes the user already exists. You'd have to either create the user and then force setup, or keep the TOTP secret temporarily until the account is created.
- **The popup:** a client component in `apps/web/modules/...` that reads `session.user.requiresTwoFactorSetup` and reuses the existing 2FA setup flow. `AdminPasswordBanner.tsx` is a good model.

## A note on the deferred design choice

The flag is written into the JWT when the user logs in. Changing `user.twoFactorEnabled` in the database later doesn't update a token that already exists. So when you decide how the popup closes, the options are roughly:
- call `useSession().update()` after setup succeeds. The `trigger === "update"` branch at [line 432](packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts#L432) would need to clear the flag.
- make the popup check the database itself instead of trusting the session.
- force the user to log in again.

That decision will also touch `next-auth-options.ts`.

```text
import { defaultResponderForAppDir } from "app/api/defaultResponderForAppDir";
import { parseRequestData } from "app/api/parseRequestData";
import { cookies, headers } from "next/headers";
import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import type { NextRequest } from "next/server";

import { ErrorCode } from "@calcom/features/auth/lib/ErrorCode";
import { getServerSession } from "@calcom/features/auth/lib/getServerSession";
import { checkRateLimitAndThrowError } from "@calcom/lib/checkRateLimitAndThrowError";
import { symmetricDecrypt } from "@calcom/lib/crypto";
import { totpAuthenticatorCheck } from "@calcom/lib/totp";
import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";

import { buildLegacyRequest } from "@lib/buildLegacyCtx";

async function postHandler(req: NextRequest) {
  const body = await parseRequestData(req);
  const session = await getServerSession({ req: buildLegacyRequest(await headers(), await cookies()) });

  if (!session) {
    return NextResponse.json({ message: "Not authenticated" }, { status: 401 });
  }

  if (!session.user?.id) {
    console.error("Session is missing a user id.");
    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.InternalServerError }, { status: 500 });
  }

  await checkRateLimitAndThrowError({
    rateLimitingType: "core",
    identifier: `api:totp-enable:${session.user.id}`,
  });

  const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: session.user.id } });
  if (!user) {
    console.error(`Session references user that no longer exists.`);
    return NextResponse.json({ message: "Not authenticated" }, { status: 401 });
  }

  if (user.twoFactorEnabled) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled }, { status: 400 });
  }

  if (!user.twoFactorSecret) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.TwoFactorSetupRequired }, { status: 400 });
  }

  if (!process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) {
    console.error("Missing encryption key; cannot proceed with two factor setup.");
    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.InternalServerError }, { status: 500 });
  }

  const secret = symmetricDecrypt(user.twoFactorSecret, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY);
  if (secret.length !== 32) {
    console.error(
      `Two factor secret decryption failed. Expected key with length 32 but got ${secret.length}`
    );
    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.InternalServerError }, { status: 500 });
  }

  const isValidToken = totpAuthenticatorCheck(body.code, secret);
  if (!isValidToken) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.IncorrectTwoFactorCode }, { status: 400 });
  }

  await prisma.user.update({
    where: {
      id: session.user.id,
    },
    data: {
      twoFactorEnabled: true,
    },
  });

  return NextResponse.json({ message: "Two-factor enabled" });
}

export const POST = defaultResponderForAppDir(postHandler);
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 18:52:54Z)**_

I compared four ways to close the popup. **Signing out and back in works, and it's the simplest to build, but I don't think it's the best.** Recalculating the flag on every session read (Option C) handles more real situations correctly, and it costs about the same per request, because that code path already runs a database query each time.

## Two facts that shape every option

**1. The flag is saved into a token when the user logs in.** Sessions use JWTs (tokens stored in the browser) with no `maxAge` set ([next-auth-options.ts:384](packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts#L384)), so next-auth's default applies: **30 days**. Anything worked out in `authorizeCredentials` stays the same for up to 30 days unless something updates it.

**2. The `jwt` callback already reads the database on every session read.** After login, each call to `getServerSession` or `/api/auth/session` arrives with no `user`, so it goes to `autoMergeIdentities()` ([line 527](packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts#L527)). That function re-reads the user from the database ([line 444](packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts#L444)). It currently copies the old token values over the fresh database values (`...existingUser, ...token`, [line 504](packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts#L504)), so a flag saved at login survives every refresh.

Some details of the existing setup flow also matter:
- `EnableTwoFactorModal` asks for the password, then shows the QR code, then asks for the code, then shows backup codes. 2FA is switched on in the database when the code is accepted ([line 139](apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx#L139)), **before** the backup codes appear. `onEnable()` only runs when the user clicks past the backup codes ([line 272](apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx#L272)).
- The setup and enable routes both reject a user who already has 2FA with `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled`.

---

## Option A: Sign out and back in

**Flow:** the user finishes setup and clicks past the backup codes. `onEnable` calls `signOut({ callbackUrl: "/auth/login" })`. They log in again with email, password and their new code. `authorizeCredentials` now sees `twoFactorEnabled: true` and doesn't set the flag.

**Pros**
- No changes to the `jwt` or `session` callbacks beyond adding the flag at login.
- The new token is guaranteed correct, because a real login builds it.
- The user proves right away that they can log in with 2FA.
- Easy to test, and easy to explain in a design doc.

**Cons**
- **Friction.** In about two minutes the user types their password three times (login, setup confirmation, login again) and enters a 2FA code twice. They also lose the page they were on, though `callbackUrl` can fix that.
- **Other devices can get stuck.** Signing out clears the cookie only in this browser. On a laptop that's still logged in, the token still has the flag, so the popup appears. The user starts setup, gets `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled`, and can't close the popup or finish. The popup has to treat that error as "sign out". The same happens if the user closes the tab on the backup-codes screen: 2FA is on in the database, the token is stale, and they're stuck on the next visit.
- **The admin switch is slow to apply in both directions.** Turning it **on** doesn't affect anyone already logged in for up to 30 days. Turning it **off** doesn't release anyone who already has the flag. Your spec only mentions users who log in, but an admin who flips a "require 2FA" switch probably expects it to apply now.
- **Backup codes can be lost if you trigger the sign-out at the wrong moment.** If you sign out when the enable request succeeds, the user never sees their backup codes. It has to run from `onEnable`.

---

## Option B: Refresh the session in place with `useSession().update()`

**Flow:** after `onEnable`, call `update()`. That runs the `trigger === "update"` branch ([line 432](packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts#L432)). You change it to re-read `twoFactorEnabled` from the database and clear the flag. The popup closes when the session updates.

**Pros**
- No sign-out. The user stays on their page.
- Small change: one database read in the update branch, plus one client call.

**Cons**
- **Security trap:** `update()` sends whatever the browser gives it, and that branch currently copies those values into the token (`name`, `email`, and others). If you follow that pattern (`requiresTwoFactorSetup: session?.requiresTwoFactorSetup`), anyone can run `update({ requiresTwoFactorSetup: false })` in the browser console and skip setup. The flag must come from the database only.
- Other devices still get stuck, the same as Option A.
- The admin switch is still only checked at login, the same as Option A.

B fixes the friction but none of A's correctness problems.

---

## Option C: Recalculate the flag from the database on every session read

**Flow:** write one helper, for example `computeRequiresTwoFactorSetup(user)`, that returns `identityProvider === CAL && !twoFactorEnabled && isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide()`. Call it in three places: `authorizeCredentials` at login, `autoMergeIdentities` on every read, and the update branch. In `autoMergeIdentities`, add `twoFactorEnabled` and `identityProvider` to the existing `select`, and set the flag *after* the `...token` copy so an old value can't win. After setup, the popup calls `update()` and closes.

**Pros**
- **Correct in every case covered above:**
  - Turning the switch on reaches logged-in users on their next page load.
  - Turning it off releases them on their next page load.
  - Other devices fix themselves: the laptop's next request sees `twoFactorEnabled: true` and the popup never appears.
  - Closing the tab on the backup-codes screen is harmless.
- **Cheap.** The user query already runs, so the new fields cost nothing extra. The feature-flag lookup only runs for CAL users *without* 2FA, so users who already have 2FA and OAuth users skip it. With the switch on, that group shrinks to nobody over time. Use the cached `getFeatureRepository()` here, not the uncached Prisma one that `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide` uses. The trade-off is that the switch then applies within the cache's lifetime rather than instantly.
- No sign-out and no repeated typing.
- The session flag can be trusted, so you could later block API calls on the server, not just in the UI.

**Cons**
- It changes code that runs on every authenticated request, so bugs there are serious. It needs unit tests on the helper and on the order of the token copy.
- More code than A or B: one helper and three call sites.
- It's slightly broader than your spec ("an existing user logs in"). Users already logged in are affected too. I think that matches what the admin switch should mean, but your team should agree on it.

---

## Option D: Don't use the session; the popup reads `viewer.me`

**Flow:** `viewer.me.get` already returns `twoFactorEnabled` and `identityProvider` ([get.handler.ts:134](packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/me/get.handler.ts#L134)). The popup opens when the switch is on, the user is a CAL user, and they don't have 2FA. After setup, invalidate the query and the popup closes.

**Pros**
- No auth changes at all. It fixes itself across devices, and the switch applies immediately.

**Cons**
- **It contradicts your spec**, which has the server mark the user at login. Nothing on the server knows the user is non-compliant, so there's nothing to enforce later. It's purely a UI check.
- The popup flashes in after the query loads, and the page also needs the switch state from somewhere.

---

## Comparison

| | A: Sign out | B: `update()` | C: Recalculate | D: Query |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Effort | Lowest | Low | Medium | Low |
| User friction after setup | High (log in again) | None | None | None |
| Other logged-in devices | Stuck unless handled | Stuck unless handled | Fixes itself | Fixes itself |
| Switch on reaches logged-in users | Up to 30 days | Up to 30 days | Next page load | Next page load |
| Switch off releases users | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| Runs on every request | No | No | Yes (cheap) | No |
| Can be enforced on the server later | Weakly | Weakly | Yes | No |
| Matches spec ("server marks at login") | Yes | Yes | Yes, and more | No |

## Recommendation

**Option C.** Its hardest part, a fresh database read on every session, already exists. In return it fixes the stuck-device problem and makes the admin switch apply both ways, and A and B both need workarounds for those.

**Option A is still a defensible choice** if you want the smallest, lowest-risk change for this sprint. If you go with it, three things are required:
1. Call `signOut` from `onEnable` (after the backup codes), not when the enable request succeeds.
2. In the popup, treat `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled` from the setup or enable routes as "sign out now", so stale devices and closed tabs can recover.
3. Write down in the design doc that the switch only applies at the next login.

One point applies to every option: the popup is only a UI barrier. Anyone can delete the overlay in the browser's dev tools and keep using the app. If the requirement is meant as real security and not a nudge, you'll eventually want a server-side check, for example tRPC middleware that rejects requests while the flag is set. Option C is the only one where the session flag is trustworthy enough to use for that.

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 18:59:49Z)**_

Mostly yes. Two parts need correcting: it isn't "in the background", and rewriting the token isn't what makes it work.

## What actually happens

**When it runs:** every time the server reads the session, not exactly on every page load. In practice that's almost every request that checks auth:
- server-rendered pages and layouts that call `getServerSession`
- tRPC calls and API routes, which read the session to find out who you are
- the browser's `useSession()`, which fetches `/api/auth/session` on mount, when the window regains focus, and when `update()` is called

A client-side navigation that never touches the session won't run it. The next tRPC call or focus refresh will.

**What it checks:**
- **The user's 2FA status comes from the live database.** It's read by the user query `autoMergeIdentities` already runs, so it's always current.
- **The site rule comes from a cache, not the database.** Use the cached `getFeatureRepository()`, not the uncached one in `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide`. The cache keeps values for up to 5 minutes, but the admin toggle writes through that same repository, and its `update()` clears the cache entry ([CachedFeatureRepository.ts:33](packages/features/flags/repositories/CachedFeatureRepository.ts#L33)). So a switch flip shows up on the next read. If the cache turns out to be per-server-instance rather than shared, other instances could lag by up to 5 minutes.
- **The site rule is only checked when it can matter:** a CAL (email and password) user without 2FA. Users who already have 2FA and Google or other OAuth users skip that lookup.

**"Updates the token in the background":** not quite.
- **It isn't in the background.** The check runs inside the request, before the page or API response is produced. It adds almost nothing, because the user query was already happening.
- **Rewriting the token isn't what makes it correct.** The flag is recalculated from scratch on every read, so whatever value is stored in the cookie is ignored. Each request gets a fresh answer.
- **The cookie does get rewritten sometimes.** When the browser hits `/api/auth/session`, next-auth saves the new token into the cookie. Server-rendered pages in the App Router can't set cookies, so there the fresh value is used for that request but not saved. That's fine, because the next read recalculates it anyway.

## Putting it together

The token is no longer where the decision lives; it just carries the result. That's why Option C fixes the problems A and B have:
- A laptop that's been logged in for a week has a token saying the flag is set. Its next request recalculates, sees `twoFactorEnabled: true`, and the popup never appears.
- When the admin flips the switch, every logged-in user picks it up on their next session read.

The one requirement in the code: in `autoMergeIdentities`, set the flag *after* the `...token` copy ([line 504](packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts#L504)). Otherwise the old value saved in the token overwrites the fresh one.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 19:04:43Z)**_

Yes, that's right. A few specifics:

- **Every request that checks auth:** yes. That covers anything that reads the session: server-rendered pages, tRPC calls, API routes, and the browser's `/api/auth/session` fetches.
- **The user's 2FA status comes from the live database:** yes. It doesn't add a query. `autoMergeIdentities` already loads the user on every session read, so you only add `twoFactorEnabled` and `identityProvider` to its existing `select`.
- **The site-wide rule comes from the cache:** yes, but only for CAL (email and password) users who don't have 2FA. Users who already have 2FA and Google or other OAuth users skip that lookup. When the admin flips the switch, the cache entry is cleared, so the next read sees the new value.

The result of those checks becomes the flag for that request, and whatever value was stored in the token is ignored.

```text
# Issue #111 -- Add an admin setting to require 2FA for all users

## Class Diagram

![Class diagram](111-kojoshuay-class.png)

## Sequence Diagram

![Sequence diagram](111-kojoshuay-sequence.png)

## Q&A

**Class diagram:**

1. Among all the classes shown in the diagram, which 1--2 are most central to understanding the codebase and solving the issue? Explain what role each one plays.

The two most important classes are `SecurityView` and `CachedFeatureRepository` 
* `SecurityView` (new client component) manages the local UI state to intercept clicks, serving as the primary frontend safeguard that forces admins to view a warning dialog before turning off 2FA
* `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide` (new helper module) embodies the core architectural design decision for this feature. It bypasses the cache to read the security state directly from the live database, establishing the foundation so that the upcoming login check never acts on stale data.

2. What is the most significant relationship shown in the diagram? Explain what it represents in the system and why it matters for understanding the solution.

The most important relationship is the separation of database reads and writes. To ensure the security policy, and by extension the admin page, never act on a cached value, the `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide` helper reads directly from the live database (`PrismaFeatureRepository`). However, when an admin saves a change, the `toggleFeatureFlag` endpoint saves through the `CachedFeatureRepository`. This ensures that whenever the setting is updated, the cache is automatically cleared so the rest of the application does not rely on old data.

3. Looking back at your implementation, is there anything in this design you would change, and why?

No, not as of this moment. 

**Sequence diagram:**

1. What user action or system event starts the sequence, and what is the expected outcome when it completes successfully?

The sequence starts when the Admin clicks the  toggle switch to 'off' inside the `SecurityView` component. The outcome is that, after the admin confirms in the warning dialog, the database updates the `enabled` field to `false` and records the admin's ID (`updatedBy`). Subsequently, the cache clears its stale keys, and the frontend updates the screen by showing a success toast, refreshing the queries, and flipping the switch to 'off'.

2. Identify the 2--3 most important steps in the sequence. For each one, describe what is happening and note whether it involves existing code or new/modified code from your solution.

* The `SecurityView` intercepts the click locally. Instead of immediately firing a network request, it halts the process to display a warning dialog, requiring confirmation from the admin (new code).
* Once the network request hits the `toggleFeatureFlag` tRPC endpoint, it runs `isAuthed` and `isAdminMiddleware`. This is the backend security checkpoint that blocks non-admins by throwing an UNAUTHORIZED error(existing code).
* After Prisma updates the database and returns the row, `@Unmemoize` runs inside `CachedFeatureRepository.update` to explicitly delete the per-flag and all-flags cache keys in Redis (existing code).

3. What error cases or alternative paths are not shown in the diagram, and why did you leave them out?

* If the network request drops or the database update fails, it triggers SecurityView's onError callback to show a "Couldn't update..." toast and revert the switch. Left out because it is a standard infrastructure edge case.
* If Redis fails during the `@Unmemoize` step, the error is caught and logged internally by the decorator (try/catch and Promise.allSettled). Left out because the error is swallowed internally. Since the database save still succeeds and no error is returned to the frontend, the network replies remain the same, making it redundant. 

**Cross-cutting:**

4. If you used AI to create or check any part of the diagrams, describe what it produced, what you verified against the actual code, and what you had to correct or add. If AI was not used, write "N/A."

I first proposed a text based outline of the feature's architecture and asked AI to create the Mermaid code for the diagrams. I then verifed the output agasint the actual codebase by analying the diagram that was created from the code and manually editing the diagram. Along the way, I asked AI to verify my edits. For example, I had to manually correct and add several details: adding conditional paths for user cancellations and non admin errros, correcting the updatedBy field to reflect the codebase, and fixing the cache clearing step to show that `@Unmemoize` runs inside `CachedFeatureRepository.update` method, not a standalone step.
```

```text
    10	import { ErrorCode } from "@calcom/features/auth/lib/ErrorCode";
    11	import { getServerSession } from "@calcom/features/auth/lib/getServerSession";
    12	import { verifyPassword } from "@calcom/features/auth/lib/verifyPassword";
    13	import { checkRateLimitAndThrowError } from "@calcom/lib/checkRateLimitAndThrowError";
    14	import { symmetricEncrypt } from "@calcom/lib/crypto";
    15	import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";
    16	import { IdentityProvider } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";
    17	
    18	import { buildLegacyRequest } from "@lib/buildLegacyCtx";
    19	
    20	async function postHandler(req: NextRequest) {
    21	  const body = await parseRequestData(req);
    22	  const session = await getServerSession({ req: buildLegacyRequest(await headers(), await cookies()) });
    23	
    24	  if (!session) {
    25	    return NextResponse.json({ message: "Not authenticated" }, { status: 401 });
    26	  }
    27	
    28	  if (!session.user?.id) {
    29	    console.error("Session is missing a user id.");
    30	    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.InternalServerError }, { status: 500 });
    31	  }
    32	
    33	  await checkRateLimitAndThrowError({
    34	    rateLimitingType: "core",
    35	    identifier: `api:totp-setup:${session.user.id}`,
    36	  });
    37	
    38	  const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: session.user.id }, include: { password: true } });
    39	
    40	  if (!user) {
    41	    console.error(`Session references user that no longer exists.`);
    42	    return NextResponse.json({ message: "Not authenticated" }, { status: 401 });
    43	  }
    44	
    45	  if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !user.password?.hash) {
    46	    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled }, { status: 400 });
    47	  }
    48	
    49	  if (!user.password?.hash) {
    50	    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.UserMissingPassword }, { status: 400 });
    51	  }
    52	
    53	  if (user.twoFactorEnabled) {
    54	    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled }, { status: 400 });
    55	  }
    56	
    57	  if (!process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) {
    58	    console.error("Missing encryption key; cannot proceed with two factor setup.");
    59	    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.InternalServerError }, { status: 500 });
    60	  }
    61	
    62	  const isCorrectPassword = await verifyPassword(body.password, user.password.hash);
    63	  if (!isCorrectPassword) {
    64	    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.IncorrectPassword }, { status: 400 });
    65	  }
    66	
    67	  // This generates a secret 32 characters in length. Do not modify the number of
    68	  // bytes without updating the sanity checks in the enable and login endpoints.
    69	  const secret = authenticator.generateSecret(20);
    70	
    71	  // Generate backup codes with 10 character length
    72	  const backupCodes = Array.from(Array(10), () => crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex"));
    73	
    74	  await prisma.user.update({
    75	    where: {
    76	      id: session.user.id,
    77	    },
    78	    data: {
    79	      backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY),
    80	      twoFactorEnabled: false,
    81	      twoFactorSecret: symmetricEncrypt(secret, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY),
    82	    },
    83	  });
    84	
    85	  const name = user.email || user.username || user.id.toString();
    86	  const keyUri = authenticator.keyuri(name, "Cal", secret);
    87	  const dataUri = await qrcode.toDataURL(keyUri);
    88	
    89	  return NextResponse.json({ secret, keyUri, dataUri, backupCodes });
    90	}
```

```text
--
## User Story

As a site admin, I want users without 2FA to be required to set it up, so that the setting actually protects every account.

## User Scenario

The setting is on. A user who logs in with a password and doesn't have 2FA sees a setup window that can't be closed. They go through the existing setup steps: confirm their password, scan the QR code, enter the 6-digit code and save their backup codes. Then they use the app normally. A new user who signs up with email and password has to complete a 2FA step during onboarding. Users who sign in with Google or another provider aren't affected. When the setting is off, nothing changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. At login, the server decides whether the user must set up 2FA and stores the result in their session. All three conditions must hold: the setting is on, the user doesn't have 2FA, and the user signs in with a password. The browser can't skip this check.

2. While setup is required, a 2FA setup window appears on every page. It reuses the existing setup steps and has no Cancel or Close button.

3. After finishing setup, the user can use the app normally.

4. When the setting is on, onboarding includes a required 2FA step for users who sign up with a password. Otherwise the step is skipped.

5. Users who sign in through Google or another identity provider are exempt, since they can't set up 2FA in cal.diy.

6. Write tests for the login rule, covering each of the three conditions, and for the onboarding step.

## Out of Scope

* Storing or toggling the setting (sub-issue 1)
* Forcing setup on users who were already logged in when the setting was turned on. The rule applies at their next login.
* A per-team version of the setting
* Changes to how 2FA itself works

<!--

-->
As a privileged user, I require the capability to enforce a two-factor authentication mandate across our general user population. Given that our platform serves as a trusted custodian of sensitive personal information, it is imperative that we proactively leverage multi-layered verification protocols to mitigate credential-compromise risk, safeguard individual accounts against unauthorized access, and foster a culture of security-first engagement, thereby protecting user data and reinforcing our commitment to best-in-class security standards.

### Describe the solution you'd like

<!--
  Provide a clear and concise description of what you want to happen.
-->
A simple toggle switch in the website configuration page to enforce 2fa for admin accounts. This would show an non-dismissable popup the next time a user logs in. If a user is creating an account with this requirement enabled, 2FA setup should be a required step.
```

```text
import type { SessionContextValue } from "next-auth/react";
import Link from "next/link";

import { useLocale } from "@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale";
import { TopBanner } from "@calcom/ui/components/top-banner";

export type AdminPasswordBannerProps = { data: SessionContextValue["data"] };

function getBannerMessageKey(reason: "both" | "password" | "2fa" | undefined): string {
  switch (reason) {
    case "password":
      return "invalid_admin_password_password_only";
    case "2fa":
      return "invalid_admin_password_2fa_only";
    case "both":
    default:
      return "invalid_admin_password";
  }
}

function getBannerAction(reason: "both" | "password" | "2fa" | undefined): { href: string; labelKey: string } {
  switch (reason) {
    case "2fa":
      return { href: "/settings/security/two-factor-auth", labelKey: "enable_2fa" };
    case "password":
    case "both":
    default:
      return { href: "/settings/security/password", labelKey: "change_password_admin" };
  }
}

function AdminPasswordBanner({ data }: AdminPasswordBannerProps) {
  const { t } = useLocale();

  if (data?.user.role !== "INACTIVE_ADMIN") return null;

  const messageKey = getBannerMessageKey(data.user.inactiveAdminReason);
  const { href, labelKey } = getBannerAction(data.user.inactiveAdminReason);

  return (
    <>
      <TopBanner
        text={t(messageKey, { user: data.user.username })}
        variant="warning"
        actions={
          <Link href={href} className="border-b border-b-black">
            {t(labelKey)}
          </Link>
        }
      />
    </>
  );
}

export default AdminPasswordBanner;
```

```text
const INITIAL_STEP = "user-settings";
const BASE_STEPS = [
  "user-settings",
  "connected-calendar",
  "connected-video",
  "setup-availability",
  "user-profile",
] as const;

type StepType = (typeof BASE_STEPS)[number];

const getStepsAndHeadersForUser = (t: TFunction) => {
  const baseHeaders: {
    title: string;
    subtitle: string[];
    skipText?: string;
  }[] = [
    {
      title: t("welcome_to_cal_header", { appName: APP_NAME }),
      subtitle: [t("we_just_need_basic_info")],
    },
    {
      title: t("connect_your_calendar"),
      subtitle: [t("connect_your_calendar_instructions")],
      skipText: t("connect_calendar_later"),
    },
    {
      title: t("connect_your_video_app"),
      subtitle: [t("connect_your_video_app_instructions")],
      skipText: t("set_up_later"),
    },
    {
      title: t("set_availability"),
      subtitle: [
        `${t("set_availability_getting_started_subtitle_1")} ${t(
          "set_availability_getting_started_subtitle_2"
        )}`,
      ],
    },
    {
      title: t("nearly_there"),
      subtitle: [t("nearly_there_instructions")],
    },
  ];

  return {
    steps: [...BASE_STEPS],
    headers: [...baseHeaders],
  };
};

const stepRouteSchema = z.object({
  step: z
    .array(
      z.enum(["user-settings", "setup-availability", "user-profile", "connected-calendar", "connected-video"])
    )
    .default([INITIAL_STEP]),
  from: z.string().optional(),
});

type PageProps = {
  hasPendingInvites: boolean;
  user: RouterOutputs["viewer"]["me"]["get"];
};

const OnboardingPage = (props: PageProps) => {
  const pathname = usePathname();
  const params = useParamsWithFallback();
  const user = props.user;
  const router = useRouter();
  const { t } = useLocale();
  const [isNextStepLoading, startTransition] = useTransition();

  const result = stepRouteSchema.safeParse({
    ...params,
    step: Array.isArray(params.step) ? params.step : [params.step],
  });

  const currentStep = result.success ? result.data.step[0] : INITIAL_STEP;
  const from = result.success ? result.data.from : "";

  //     }

  const { steps, headers } = getStepsAndHeadersForUser(t);
  const stepTransform = (step: StepType) => {
    const stepIndex = steps.indexOf(step as (typeof steps)[number]);

    if (stepIndex > -1) {
      return steps[stepIndex];
    }
    return INITIAL_STEP;
  };
  const currentStepIndex = steps.indexOf(currentStep);

  const goToStep = (step: number) => {
    const newStep = steps[step];
    startTransition(() => {
      router.push(`/getting-started/${stepTransform(newStep)}`);
    });
  };

  const goToNextStep = (wasSkipped: boolean = false) => {
    posthog.capture("onboarding_step_completed", {
      step: currentStep,
      step_index: currentStepIndex,
      from: from,
      was_skipped: wasSkipped,
    });
    const nextIndex = currentStepIndex + 1;
    const newStep = steps[nextIndex];
    startTransition(() => {
      router.push(`/getting-started/${stepTransform(newStep)}`);
    });
  };

  return (
    <div
      className={classNames(
        "text-emphasis min-h-screen [--cal-brand:#111827] dark:[--cal-brand:#FFFFFF]",
        "[--cal-brand-emphasis:#101010] dark:[--cal-brand-emphasis:#e1e1e1]",

        "[--cal-brand-text:#FFFFFF]  dark:[--cal-brand-text:#000000]",
        "[--cal-brand-accent:#FFFFFF] dark:[--cal-brand-accent:#000000]"
      )}
      data-testid="onboarding"
      key={pathname}>
```

```text
export async function authorizeCredentials(
  credentials: Record<"email" | "password" | "totpCode" | "backupCode", string> | undefined
): Promise<User | null> {
  log.debug("CredentialsProvider:credentials:authorize", safeStringify({ credentials }));
  if (!credentials) {
    console.error(`For some reason credentials are missing`);
    throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError);
  }

  const userRepo = new UserRepository(prisma);
  const user = await userRepo.findByEmailAndIncludeProfilesAndPassword({
    email: credentials.email,
  });
  // Don't leak information about it being username or password that is invalid
  if (!user) {
    throw new Error(ErrorCode.IncorrectEmailPassword);
  }

  // Locked users cannot login
  if (user.locked) {
    throw new Error(ErrorCode.UserAccountLocked);
  }

  await checkRateLimitAndThrowError({
    identifier: hashEmail(user.email),
  });

  // Users without a password must use their identity provider (Google/SAML) to login
  if (!user.password?.hash) {
    throw new Error(ErrorCode.IncorrectEmailPassword);
  }

  // Always verify password for users who have one
  const isCorrectPassword = await verifyPassword(credentials.password, user.password.hash);
  if (!isCorrectPassword) {
    throw new Error(ErrorCode.IncorrectEmailPassword);
  }

  if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode) {
    if (!process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) {
      console.error("Missing encryption key; cannot proceed with backup code login.");
      throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError);
    }

    if (!user.backupCodes) throw new Error(ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes);

    const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY));

    // check if user-supplied code matches one
    const index = backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""));
    if (index === -1) throw new Error(ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode);

    // delete verified backup code and re-encrypt remaining
    backupCodes[index] = null;
    await prisma.user.update({
      where: {
        id: user.id,
      },
      data: {
        backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY),
      },
    });
  } else if (user.twoFactorEnabled) {
    if (!credentials.totpCode) {
      throw new Error(ErrorCode.SecondFactorRequired);
    }

    if (!user.twoFactorSecret) {
      console.error(`Two factor is enabled for user ${user.id} but they have no secret`);
      throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError);
    }

    if (!process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) {
      console.error(`"Missing encryption key; cannot proceed with two factor login."`);
      throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError);
    }

    const secret = symmetricDecrypt(user.twoFactorSecret, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY);
    if (secret.length !== 32) {
      console.error(
        `Two factor secret decryption failed. Expected key with length 32 but got ${secret.length}`
      );
      throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError);
    }

    const isValidToken = (await import("@calcom/lib/totp")).totpAuthenticatorCheck(
      credentials.totpCode,
      secret
    );
    if (!isValidToken) {
      throw new Error(ErrorCode.IncorrectTwoFactorCode);
    }
  }
  // Check if the user you are logging into has any active teams
  const hasActiveTeams = checkIfUserBelongsToActiveTeam(user);

  // authentication success- but does it meet the minimum password requirements?
  const validateRole = (role: UserPermissionRole) => {
    // User's role is not "ADMIN"
    if (role !== UserPermissionRole.ADMIN) return role;
    // User's identity provider is not "CAL"
    if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL) return role;

    if (process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E) {
      console.warn("E2E testing is enabled, skipping password and 2FA requirements for Admin");
      return role;
    }

    // User's password is valid and two-factor authentication is enabled
    if (isPasswordValid(credentials.password, false, true) && user.twoFactorEnabled) return role;
    // Code is running in a development environment
    if (isENVDev) return role;
    // By this point it is an ADMIN without valid security conditions
    return "INACTIVE_ADMIN";
  };

  const role = validateRole(user.role);
  const baseUser = AdapterUserPresenter.fromCalUser(user, role, hasActiveTeams);

  if (role === "INACTIVE_ADMIN") {
    const passwordValid = isPasswordValid(credentials.password, false, true);
    const has2FA = user.twoFactorEnabled;

    let reason: "both" | "password" | "2fa";

    if (!passwordValid && !has2FA) {
      reason = "both";
    } else if (!passwordValid) {
      reason = "password";
    } else {
      reason = "2fa";
    }

    return { ...baseUser, inactiveAdminReason: reason };
  }

  return baseUser;
}
```

```text
export const generateMetadata = async ({ params }: ServerPageProps) => {

  const step = stepParam && Array.isArray(stepParam) ? stepParam.join("/") : "";
  return await _generateMetadata(
    (t) => `${APP_NAME} - ${t("getting_started")}`,

    true,

const ServerPage = async ({ params, searchParams }: ServerPageProps) => {
  const session = await getServerSession({ req: buildLegacyRequest(await headers(), await cookies()) });

  if (!session?.user?.id) {
    return redirect("/auth/login");
  }

  const userRepo = new UserRepository(prisma);
  const meCaller = await createRouterCaller(meRouter);

  const [userTeams, user] = await Promise.all([
    userRepo.findUserTeams({
      id: session.user.id,
    }),
    meCaller.get(),
  ]);

  if (!userTeams || !user) {
    return redirect("/auth/login");
  }

  return <Page user={user} hasPendingInvites={!!userTeams.teams.find((team) => team.accepted === false)} />;
};

export default ServerPage;
```

```text
import { Authenticator, TOTP } from "@otplib/core";
import type { AuthenticatorOptions } from "@otplib/core/authenticator";
import type { TOTPOptions } from "@otplib/core/totp";
import { createDigest, createRandomBytes } from "@otplib/plugin-crypto";
import { keyDecoder, keyEncoder } from "@otplib/plugin-thirty-two";

/**
 * Checks the validity of a TOTP token using a base32-encoded secret.
 *
 * @param token - The token.
 * @param secret - The base32-encoded shared secret.
 * @param opts - The AuthenticatorOptions object.
 * @param opts.window - The amount of past and future tokens considered valid. Either a single value or array of `[past, future]`. Default: `[1, 0]`
 */
export const totpAuthenticatorCheck = (
  token: string,
  secret: string,
  opts: Partial<AuthenticatorOptions> = {}
) => {
  const { window = [1, 0], ...rest } = opts;
  const authenticator = new Authenticator({
    createDigest,
    createRandomBytes,
    keyDecoder,
    keyEncoder,
    window,
    ...rest,
  });
  return authenticator.check(token, secret);
};

import { mockDeep, mockReset, type DeepMockProxy } from "vitest-mock-extended";

import type { PrismaClient } from "@calcom/prisma";

// Prisma mock instance (singleton)
export const prismaMock: DeepMockProxy<PrismaClient> = mockDeep<PrismaClient>();

export function resetPrismaMock(): void {
  mockReset(prismaMock);
}

// Custom P2002 error class for testing unique constraint violations
export class MockPrismaClientKnownRequestError extends Error {
  code: string;
  meta?: { target?: string[] };

  constructor(message: string, { code, meta }: { code: string; meta?: { target?: string[] } }) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "PrismaClientKnownRequestError";
    this.code = code;
    this.meta = meta;
  }
}

export function createPrismaMock(): {
  default: DeepMockProxy<PrismaClient>;
  prisma: DeepMockProxy<PrismaClient>;
  Prisma: { PrismaClientKnownRequestError: typeof MockPrismaClientKnownRequestError };
} {
  return {
    default: prismaMock,
    prisma: prismaMock,
    Prisma: { PrismaClientKnownRequestError: MockPrismaClientKnownRequestError },
  };
}

// P2002 error factories
export function createP2002Error(target: string[]): MockPrismaClientKnownRequestError {
  return new MockPrismaClientKnownRequestError("Unique constraint failed", {
    code: "P2002",
    meta: { target },
  });
}

export function createP2002ErrorWithoutTarget(): MockPrismaClientKnownRequestError {
  return new MockPrismaClientKnownRequestError("Unique constraint failed", {
    code: "P2002",
    meta: {},
  });
}

export function createGenericPrismaError(): MockPrismaClientKnownRequestError {
  return new MockPrismaClientKnownRequestError("Record not found", {
    code: "P2025",
    meta: {},
  });
}
```

```text
import { getFeatureRepository } from "@calcom/features/di/containers/FeatureRepository";

export class OnboardingPathService {
  static async getGettingStartedPath(): Promise<string> {
    const featureRepository = getFeatureRepository();
    const onboardingV3Enabled = await featureRepository.checkIfFeatureIsEnabledGlobally("onboarding-v3");
    return onboardingV3Enabled ? "/onboarding/getting-started" : "/getting-started";
  }

  static async getGettingStartedPathWhenInvited(): Promise<string> {
    const featureRepository = getFeatureRepository();
    const onboardingV3Enabled = await featureRepository.checkIfFeatureIsEnabledGlobally("onboarding-v3");
    return onboardingV3Enabled ? "/onboarding/personal/settings" : "/getting-started";
  }

  static async getGettingStartedPathWithParams(queryParams?: Record<string, string>): Promise<string> {
    const basePath = await OnboardingPathService.getGettingStartedPath();

    if (!queryParams || Object.keys(queryParams).length === 0) {
      return basePath;
    }

    const params = new URLSearchParams(queryParams);
    return `${basePath}?${params.toString()}`;
  }
}

import dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";
import { FeaturesRepository } from "@calcom/features/flags/features.repository";
import { MembershipRepository } from "@calcom/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository";
import { ProfileRepository } from "@calcom/features/profile/repositories/ProfileRepository";
import { UserRepository } from "@calcom/features/users/repositories/UserRepository";
import { prisma } from "@calcom/prisma";

const ONBOARDING_INTRODUCED_AT = dayjs("September 1 2021").toISOString();

/**
 * Checks if a user needs onboarding on the server side.
 * Returns the onboarding path if redirect is needed, null otherwise.
 *
 * @param userId - The user ID to check
 * @param options - Optional configuration
 * @param options.checkEmailVerification - Whether to check if email verification is required
 * @param options.organizationId - Optional organizationId from session (to avoid extra query)
 */
export async function checkOnboardingRedirect(
  userId: number,
  options?: {
    checkEmailVerification?: boolean;
    organizationId?: number | null;
  }
): Promise<string | null> {
  // Query user data needed for onboarding check using UserRepository
  const userRepository = new UserRepository(prisma);
  const user = await userRepository.findById({ id: userId });

  if (!user) {
    return null;
  }

  // Use provided organizationId or query it via ProfileRepository
  let organizationId: number | null;
  if (options?.organizationId !== undefined) {
    organizationId = options.organizationId;
  } else {
    const profile = await ProfileRepository.findFirstForUserId({ userId });
    organizationId = profile?.organizationId ?? null;
  }

  // Check if user should be shown onboarding
  const shouldShowOnboarding =
    !user.completedOnboarding && !organizationId && dayjs(user.createdDate).isAfter(ONBOARDING_INTRODUCED_AT);

  if (!shouldShowOnboarding) {
    return null;
  }

  // Check email verification if needed
  const featuresRepository = new FeaturesRepository(prisma);

  if (options?.checkEmailVerification) {
    const emailVerificationEnabled =
      await featuresRepository.checkIfFeatureIsEnabledGlobally("email-verification");

    if (!user.emailVerified && user.identityProvider === "CAL" && emailVerificationEnabled) {
      // User needs email verification, redirect to verification page
      return "/auth/verify-email";
```

```text
import { createRouterCaller } from "app/_trpc/context";
import type { PageProps } from "app/_types";
import { _generateMetadata } from "app/_utils";
import { notFound } from "next/navigation";
import { z } from "zod";

import { availabilityRouter } from "@calcom/trpc/server/routers/viewer/availability/_router";
import { travelSchedulesRouter } from "@calcom/trpc/server/routers/viewer/travelSchedules/_router";

import { AvailabilitySettingsWebWrapper } from "~/availability/[schedule]/schedule-view";

const querySchema = z.object({
  schedule: z
    .string()
    .refine((val) => !isNaN(Number(val)), {
      message: "schedule must be a string that can be cast to a number",
    })
    .transform((val) => Number(val)),
});

export const generateMetadata = async () => {
  return await _generateMetadata(
    (t) => t("availability"),
    () => "",
    undefined,
    undefined,
    "/availability"
  );
```

```text
import { redirect } from "next/navigation";

import { FeaturesRepository } from "@calcom/features/flags/features.repository";
import { prisma } from "@calcom/prisma";

export default async function OnboardingLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const featuresRepository = new FeaturesRepository(prisma);
  const isOnboardingV3Enabled = await featuresRepository.checkIfFeatureIsEnabledGlobally("onboarding-v3");

  if (!isOnboardingV3Enabled) {
    redirect("/getting-started");
  }

  return <>{children}</>;
}

export const generateMetadata = async () => {

    undefined,
    "/onboarding/personal/calendar"
  );

const ServerPage = async () => {
  const session = await getServerSession({ req: buildLegacyRequest(await headers(), await cookies()) });

  if (!session?.user?.id) {
    return redirect("/auth/login");
  }

  const userEmail = session.user.email || "";

  return <PersonalCalendarView userEmail={userEmail} />;
};

export default ServerPage;

page.tsx
import { useRouter } from "next/navigation";

import { useLocale } from "@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale";
import { sessionStorage } from "@calcom/lib/webstorage";
import { trpc } from "@calcom/trpc/react";
import { showToast } from "@calcom/ui/components/toast";
import { setShowWelcomeToCalcomModalFlag } from "@calcom/web/modules/shell/hooks/useWelcomeToCalcomModal";

const ONBOARDING_REDIRECT_KEY = "onBoardingRedirect";
const ORG_MODAL_STORAGE_KEY = "showNewOrgModal";

const DEFAULT_EVENT_TYPES = [
  {
    title: "15min_meeting",
    slug: "15min",
    length: 15,
  },
  {
    title: "30min_meeting",
    slug: "30min",
    length: 30,
  },
  {
    title: "secret_meeting",
    slug: "secret",
    length: 15,
    hidden: true,
  },
];

export const useSubmitPersonalOnboarding = () => {
  const router = useRouter();
  const { t } = useLocale();
  const utils = trpc.useUtils();

  const { data: eventTypes } = trpc.viewer.eventTypes.list.useQuery();
  const createEventType = trpc.viewer.eventTypesHeavy.create.useMutation();

  const mutation = trpc.viewer.me.updateProfile.useMutation({
    onSuccess: async () => {
      try {
        // Create default event types if user has none
        if (eventTypes?.length === 0) {
          await Promise.all(
            DEFAULT_EVENT_TYPES.map(async (event) => {
              return createEventType.mutateAsync({
                title: t(event.title),
                slug: event.slug,
                length: event.length,
                hidden: event.hidden,
              });
            })
          );
        }
      } catch (error) {
        console.error(error);
      }

      await utils.viewer.me.get.refetch();

      const redirectUrl = localStorage.getItem(ONBOARDING_REDIRECT_KEY);
      if (redirectUrl) {
        localStorage.removeItem(ONBOARDING_REDIRECT_KEY);
        router.push(redirectUrl);
        return;
      }

      // Check if org modal flag is set - if so, don't show personal modal
      // Organization onboarding takes precedence
      const hasOrgModalFlag = sessionStorage.getItem(ORG_MODAL_STORAGE_KEY) === "true";

      if (!hasOrgModalFlag) {
        // Only set personal modal flag if org modal flag is not set
        setShowWelcomeToCalcomModalFlag();
        router.push("/event-types?welcomeToCalcomModal=true");
      } else {
        // Org modal flag exists - redirect to event-types without personal modal query param
        // The org modal will show via sessionStorage check
        router.push("/event-types?newOrganizationModal=true");
      }
    },
    onError: (error) => {
      showToast(t("something_went_wrong"), "error");
      console.error(error);
    },
  });

  const submitPersonalOnboarding = () => {
    // telemetry.event(telemetryEventTypes.onboardingFinished);
    mutation.mutate({
      completedOnboarding: true,
    });
  };

  return {
    submitPersonalOnboarding,
    isSubmitting: mutation.isPending,
  };
};
```

```text
    27	const TwoFactorAuthView = () => {

    29	  const { data: sessionData } = useSession();
    30	
    31	  const { t } = useLocale();
    32	  const { data: user, isPending } = trpc.viewer.me.get.useQuery({ includePasswordAdded: true });

    45	        toggleSwitchAtTheEnd={true}
    46	        data-testid="two-factor-switch"
    47	        title={t("two_factor_auth")}
    48	        description={t("add_an_extra_layer_of_security")}
    49	        checked={user?.twoFactorEnabled ?? false}
    50	        onCheckedChange={() =>
```

```text
    14	const enum DIALOG_STATE {
    15	  // Dialog is there in the DOM but not visible.
    16	  CLOSED = "CLOSED",
    17	  // State from the time b/w the Dialog is dismissed and the time the "dialog" query param is removed from the URL.
    18	  CLOSING = "CLOSING",
    19	  // Dialog is visible.
    20	  OPEN = "OPEN",
    21	}
    22	
    23	export function Dialog(props: DialogProps) {
    24	  const isPlatform = useIsPlatform();
    25	  return !isPlatform ? <ControlledDialog {...props} /> : <DialogPrimitive.Dialog {...props} />;
    26	}
    27	
    28	function ControlledDialog(props: DialogProps) {
    29	  const router = useRouter();
    30	  const pathname = usePathname();
    31	  const searchParams = useCompatSearchParams();
    32	  const newSearchParams = new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString());
    33	  const { children, name, ...dialogProps } = props;
    34	
    35	  // only used if name is set
    36	  const [dialogState, setDialogState] = useState(dialogProps.open ? DIALOG_STATE.OPEN : DIALOG_STATE.CLOSED);
    37	  const shouldOpenDialog = newSearchParams.get("dialog") === name;
    38	  if (name) {
    39	    const clearQueryParamsOnClose = ["dialog", ...(props.clearQueryParamsOnClose || [])];
    40	    dialogProps.onOpenChange = (open) => {
    41	      if (props.onOpenChange) {
    42	        props.onOpenChange(open);
    43	      }
    44	
    45	      // toggles "dialog" query param
    46	      if (open) {
    47	        newSearchParams.set("dialog", name);
    48	      } else {
    49	        clearQueryParamsOnClose.forEach((queryParam) => {
    50	          newSearchParams.delete(queryParam);
    51	        });
    52	        router.push(`${pathname}?${newSearchParams.toString()}`);
    53	      }
    54	      setDialogState(open ? DIALOG_STATE.OPEN : DIALOG_STATE.CLOSING);
    55	    };
    56	
    57	    if (dialogState === DIALOG_STATE.CLOSED && shouldOpenDialog) {
    58	      setDialogState(DIALOG_STATE.OPEN);
    59	    }
    60	
    61	    if (dialogState === DIALOG_STATE.CLOSING && !shouldOpenDialog) {
    62	      setDialogState(DIALOG_STATE.CLOSED);
    63	    }
    64	
    65	    // allow overriding
    66	    if (!("open" in dialogProps)) {
    67	      dialogProps.open = dialogState === DIALOG_STATE.OPEN ? true : false;
    68	    }
    69	  }
    70	
    71	  return <BaseDialog {...dialogProps}>{children}</BaseDialog>;
```

I traced the whole signup flow. Today nothing on the signup path or in the credentials login reads `REQUIRE_TWO_FACTOR_AUTH_FLAG`. The only places that use the flag or `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide` are the admin security page, `apps/web/modules/settings/admin/security-view.tsx`, `FlagAdminList.tsx`, the config, and the helper and its test.

## 1. Signup UI
- **Page:** `/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy/apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/signup/page.tsx`
- **View:** `/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy/apps/web/modules/signup-view.tsx`. It's a client component, and there's a `signup-view.test.tsx` next to it.
- **Form schema (lines 56-59):** the API `signupSchema` from `packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts:849` (username optional, email, password, language, token), extended with `apiError` and `cfToken`. Lines 218-230 add a refinement that makes username required unless it's an org invite by link.
- **Fields:**
  - Username (lines 542-558): has a debounced availability and premium check through `fetchUsername`.
  - Email (561-570).
  - Password (573-580): hints are `caplow`, `min`, `num`.
  - Optional Cloudflare Turnstile (582-596).
  - Cookie-consent checkbox (598-602).
  - Submit button (611-625).
- **Email-form toggle:** the form only shows when `displayEmailForm` is true (it starts as `token`). Otherwise you get the Google, Microsoft and "continue with email" buttons (629-765).
- **Submit, `signUp` (270-376):** calls `fetchSignup({...data, language, token}, cfToken)`.
  - `fetchSignup` (`/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy/packages/features/auth/signup/lib/fetchSignup.ts:28-82`) POSTs JSON to `/api/auth/signup`, adds UTM params to the URL and sends a `cf-access-token` header.
  - It returns `{ok, data}` or `{ok:false, status, error}`. Helpers: `isUserAlreadyExistsError` (409), `hasCheckoutSession`, `isAccountUnderReview`.
- **After submit:**
  - 409 "user exists": shows a toast, then `router.push('/auth/login?callbackUrl=...')` after 3s (292-299).
  - Checkout session: Stripe redirect (301-310).
  - `accountUnderReview`: shows the under-review panel (315-318).
  - If `emailVerificationEnabled && !token && !isOrgInviteByLink`: saves username, email and password to `sessionStorage[SIGNUP_DRAFT_KEY]` (324-333).
  - Then it always signs in automatically with `signIn("credentials", {...data, callbackUrl})` (353-356). The callback is `${WEBAPP_URL}/auth/verify-email?from=signup` if email verification is on, otherwise `/getting-started` or `/onboarding/getting-started` (when `onboardingV3Enabled`). If a `callbackUrl` query param is present it wins (335-351).
  - Only email, password, username and language are passed to `signIn`. No `totpCode`.

## 2. Server handlers
- **Route:** `/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy/apps/web/app/api/auth/signup/route.ts`. It rate-limits per IP (44-47), checks Turnstile (51-54), and runs `ensureSignupIsEnabled` (18-37: `disable-signup` flag or `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_SIGNUP`, skipped when there's a token).
- **Which handler runs (lines 65-69):** `if (IS_PREMIUM_USERNAME_ENABLED) calcomSignupHandler else selfHostedSignupHandler`.
  - `IS_PREMIUM_USERNAME_ENABLED` (`packages/lib/constants.ts:170-172`) = `(IS_CALCOM || (NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E && IS_STRIPE_ENABLED)) && NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PREMIUM_PLAN_PRICE_MONTHLY`.
  - `IS_CALCOM` (54-60) is true only when the hostname ends in cal.com, cal.dev, cal.qa, cal-staging.com or cal.eu. So a self-hosted instance runs **`selfHostedHandler`**.
- **`/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy/apps/web/app/api/auth/signup/handlers/selfHostedHandler.ts`:**
  - Parses `signupSchema` (27), `slugify`s the username and lowercases the email.
  - **No-token path:** `validateAndGetCorrectedUsernameAndEmail` (60-72), `hashPassword` (75), `isUsernameReservedDueToMigration` (158), then `getUserRepository().create({username, email, hashedPassword, organizationId:null, creationSource: WEBAPP, identityProvider: CAL, locked:false})` (163-171).
    - No `emailVerified` is set.
    - P2002 errors return 409.
    - Then `prefillAvatar` (if the env vars are set) and `sendEmailVerification` (187-191).
  - **Token/team path:** `userRepository.upsertForSignup({..., emailVerified: new Date(), identityProvider: CAL})` (119-126), then `createOrUpdateMemberships`, `joinAnyChildTeamOnOrgInvite`, and deletes the verification token.
  - Returns `201 {message:"Created user"}` (194). It never returns any user id or secret.
- **`UserRepository.create`** (`/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy/packages/features/users/repositories/UserRepository.ts:905-965`): `prisma.user.create` with a nested `password.create`, a default schedule with availability, `creationSource`, `locked`, an org profile when there's an org, and `...rest` spread in. So extra Prisma `UserCreateInput` fields such as `twoFactorSecret` would pass through.
- **`upsertForSignup`:** lines 1557-1598.
- **`calcomSignupHandler.ts`:** same structure, wrapped in `usernameHandler`. It adds a stubbed `billingService`, the watchlist lock, a premium-username 402/418 path, and the `signup-watchlist-review` flag (281-306). It sends verification email only when there's no checkout and no token (308-314).
- **Is email verification required before login?** No, not at login. `authorizeCredentials` (`/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy/packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:151-288`) never checks `emailVerified`.
  - The check happens after login, in `packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts:54-61`. When the `email-verification` flag is on, `!emailVerified` and the provider is CAL, it redirects to `/auth/verify-email`. That check is used by `apps/web/app/page.tsx` and `event-types/page.tsx`.
  - `sendEmailVerification` (`packages/features/auth/lib/verifyEmail.ts:32`, flag check at 43) only sends when that flag is on.
- **Login 2FA (same file):**
  - If `twoFactorEnabled` and there's no `totpCode`, it throws `SecondFactorRequired` (213-215).
  - It decrypts `twoFactorSecret` with `symmetricDecrypt` and requires the result to be 32 characters (226-232).
  - It checks the code with `totpAuthenticatorCheck` from `@calcom/lib/totp` (236-242).
  - Backup codes are handled at 189-212.

## 3. Server-side props
- `page.tsx` (21-27) calls `withAppDirSsr(getServerSideProps)` with `buildLegacyCtx(headers, cookies, params, searchParams)` and spreads the result into `<Signup {...props} />`.
- `SignupProps = inferSSRProps<typeof getServerSideProps>` (`signup-view.tsx:67`), so a new prop added in gSSP flows into the view's type automatically.
- **`/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy/apps/web/lib/signup/getServerSideProps.tsx`:**
  - Already reads global flags with `new FeaturesRepository(prisma).checkIfFeatureIsEnabledGlobally(...)`: `email-verification`, `disable-signup`, `onboarding-v3` (24-29).
  - Redirects users who are already logged in (43-54) and handles signup-disabled (65-72).
  - The base `props` object (56-63) holds `redirectUrl`, `isGoogleLoginEnabled`, `prepopulateFormValues`, `emailVerificationEnabled` and `onboardingV3Enabled`.
  - It's returned through `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))` on the no-token path (75-88), and with `token`, `orgSlug` and `orgAutoAcceptEmail` on the token path (196-221).
  - The view also destructures `isOutlookLoginEnabled` (198), but gSSP never sets it.

## 4. TOTP setup server code
- **`/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy/apps/web/app/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup/route.ts`:**
  - It needs a session (22-31), applies a rate limit, loads the user with their password, requires a CAL provider or a password hash, requires 2FA not already enabled, and requires `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (38-60). It also verifies `body.password` (62-65).
  - **Secret:** `authenticator.generateSecret(20)` from `"otplib"` (line 7 import, line 69). This gives a 32-character base32 secret, and the comment says the 32-character length is checked in the enable and login endpoints.
  - **Backup codes:** `Array.from(Array(10), () => crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex"))` using `node:crypto` (72).
  - **Saves:** `prisma.user.update` with `backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), KEY)`, `twoFactorEnabled:false`, `twoFactorSecret: symmetricEncrypt(secret, KEY)` (74-83). `symmetricEncrypt` comes from `@calcom/lib/crypto`.
  - **QR:** `authenticator.keyuri(email||username||id, "Cal", secret)` and `qrcode.toDataURL(keyUri)` (85-87).
  - **Returns:** `{secret, keyUri, dataUri, backupCodes}`.
  - The only user-specific inputs are the session id and the label name. Generating the secret and backup codes doesn't depend on a user row.
- **`enable/route.ts`:**
  - Decrypts the secret and checks it's 32 characters (53-54).
  - Checks the code with `totpAuthenticatorCheck(body.code, secret)` (61), then sets `twoFactorEnabled: true` (71).
- **`/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy/packages/lib/totp.ts`:** `totpAuthenticatorCheck(token, secret, opts)` uses `@otplib/core` Authenticator with plugin-crypto and thirty-two, default `window [1,0]`.

## 5. Handler tests
- **`/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy/apps/web/app/api/auth/signup/handlers/selfHostedHandler.test.ts`** uses Vitest. Each dependency gets a module-level `vi.mock`:
  - `next/server` is mocked with `createNextServerMock()`.
  - `@calcom/prisma` and `@calcom/prisma/client` are mocked with `createPrismaMock()` (a `vitest-mock-extended` `mockDeep<PrismaClient>` singleton).
  - Simple `vi.fn` mocks cover logger, `hashPassword` (returns "hashed"), `slugify`, `constants` (`IS_PREMIUM_USERNAME_ENABLED:false`), `isUsernameReservedDueToMigration`, `sendEmailVerification`, `createOrUpdateMemberships`, `validateAndGetCorrectedUsernameAndEmail` (returns `{isValid:true, username:"testuser"}`), `joinAnyChildTeamOnOrgInvite`, `prefillAvatar`, and the token utils (delegating to hoisted `Mock`s).
  - `getUserRepository` is **not** mocked, so the real `UserRepository` runs against `prismaMock`. Assertions target `prismaMock.user.create` and `prismaMock.user.upsert`.
  - The handler is imported after the mocks, and the file runs the shared `runP2002TestSuite(name, callHandler, setupMocks)`.
- **Shared helpers** in `/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy/packages/features/auth/signup/handlers/__tests__/`:
  - `mocks/prisma.mocks.ts`: `prismaMock`, `resetPrismaMock`, `createP2002Error(target)`, `createP2002ErrorWithoutTarget`, `createGenericPrismaError`.
  - `mocks/next.mocks.ts`: NextResponse and headers mocks, plus the `MockResponse` type.
  - `mocks/signup.factories.ts`: `createSignupBody`, `createMockUser`, `createMockTeam`, `createMockFoundToken`, and the `SignupBody` type.
  - `p2002.test-suite.ts`: the 409/rethrow contract for the token and non-token paths.
- **`calcomSignupHandler.test.ts`** follows the same pattern and additionally mocks `next/headers`, `constants` (`WEBAPP_URL`), tracking, stripe utils, `getLocaleFromRequest`, the watchlist modules, `@calcom/features/di/containers/FeatureRepository`, and `buildLegacyCtx`.
- **Other tests:** `packages/features/auth/signup/lib/fetchSignup.test.ts`, `apps/web/modules/signup-view.test.tsx`, and the e2e test `apps/web/playwright/signup.e2e.ts`.

Paths below are relative to `/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy`.

## 1. Where AdminPasswordBanner renders and how it gets the session

**The render chain:**
- `apps/web/modules/shell/Shell.tsx:31` calls `useBanners()`.
- `:45` renders `{banners && <BannerContainer banners={banners} />}` inside `Layout`. The same file also mounts `<TimezoneChangeDialog />` and `<DynamicModals />` at `:41-42`, which is the existing place where global dialogs are mounted.
- `apps/web/modules/shell/banners/LayoutBanner.tsx:32,50-52` maps the `adminPasswordBanner` key to `<AdminPasswordBanner data={...}/>`.

**How the session arrives:** the banner takes it as a prop, `data: SessionContextValue["data"]` (`AdminPasswordBanner.tsx:7`). The prop comes from `useSession()` in `apps/web/modules/shell/banners/useBanners.ts:11`. Line 19 sets `adminPasswordBanner: isUserInactiveAdmin ? userSession : null`. Line 13 returns null until both the tRPC `getUserTopBanners` query and the session have loaded.

**Shell's own logic:** `Shell()` (`Shell.tsx:111-124`) calls `useRedirectToLoginIfUnauthenticated` and `useRedirectToOnboardingIfNeeded`. With `isPublic` it renders `PublicShell`, which uses the same `Layout`, so banners show there too.

**Pages that use Shell:**
- `(main-nav)/layout.tsx:17` wraps everything in `<Shell withoutMain>`: availability list, bookings, booking/[uid], event-types list, members.
- Settings: `settings/(settings-layout)/SettingsLayoutAppDirClient.tsx:549`. The admin layout (`settings/(admin-layout)/layout.tsx:24`) reuses `SettingsLayoutAppDir`.
- Event type detail: `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx:27,100`.
- Availability detail: `packages/platform/atoms/availability/AvailabilitySettings.tsx:51,399-402`.
- Also: the apps views (`components/apps/layouts/AppsLayout.tsx`, `InstalledAppsLayout.tsx`, `App.tsx`, `modules/apps/categories/*`), `refer/page.tsx`, `modules/upgrade/upgrade-view.tsx`, `modules/more/more-page-view.tsx`.

**Authenticated pages without Shell:**
- `/getting-started/[[...step]]` (`app/(use-page-wrapper)/getting-started/[[...step]]/page.tsx`) checks the session on the server and redirects, but renders `onboarding-view` with no Shell. No Shell reference exists under `apps/web/modules/getting-started`.
- `/onboarding/*` (`onboarding/layout.tsx` is just `<>{children}</>`, gated on the `onboarding-v3` flag). Pages like `onboarding/getting-started/page.tsx` and `onboarding/personal/*` check the session themselves and don't use Shell.
- Not individually checked: `video`, `payment`, `availability/troubleshoot` (it has its own layout), `auth`, `signup`, `maintenance`, `enterprise`.
- Everything under `(use-page-wrapper)` goes through `layout.tsx`, then `PageWrapperAppDir`, which wraps both Shell and non-Shell pages.

## 2. The two EnableTwoFactorModal components

| | `components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` | `components/security/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` |
|---|---|---|
| Props | `open`, `onOpenChange: () => void`, `onCancel`, `onEnable` (`:18-31`) | `onCancel`, `onEnable` only (`:18-28`) |
| Steps | ConfirmPassword, DisplayQrCode, EnterTotpCode, DisplayBackupCodes (`:33-38`) | ConfirmPassword, DisplayQrCode, EnterTotpCode (no backup codes) |
| Dialog | `<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>` (`:170`); `DialogContent type="creation"` with title and description | `<Dialog open={true}>` with no `onOpenChange` (`:146`); `TwoFactorModalHeader` |
| Password field | `PasswordField` | raw `<input>` |
| When enable succeeds | moves to the backup codes step; the Close button there calls `onEnable()` (`:264-275`) | calls `onEnable()` right away (`:117`) |
| Cancel button | `DialogFooter`, shown on every step except backup codes (`:225-234`) | always shown (`:212-214`) |
| Used by | `apps/web/modules/settings/security/two-factor-auth-view.tsx:10,61-77` | `apps/web/components/security/TwoFactorAuthSection.tsx:8,38`. Nothing imports `TwoFactorAuthSection` (grep found no other references), so this pair looks like dead code |

- `two-factor-auth-view.tsx` passes the toggle `onOpenChange={() => setEnableModalOpen(!enableModalOpen)}`. Its `onEnable` (`:64-73`) calls `signOut({callbackUrl:"/auth/login"})` when `role === "INACTIVE_ADMIN`; otherwise it calls `utils.viewer.me.invalidate()`.
- Both import `Dialog` from `@calcom/features/components/controlled-dialog`.

**Dialog internals:**
- `packages/features/components/controlled-dialog/index.tsx` is a thin wrapper. It handles the `name`/`?dialog=` query param and then renders `BaseDialog` from `@calcom/ui/components/dialog`. On platform it renders the Radix Root directly.
- `packages/ui/components/dialog/Dialog.tsx`:
  - `Dialog` (`:35-38`) is a plain `DialogPrimitive.Root`.
  - `DialogContent` props (`:40-53`): `type`, `title`, `description`, `closeText`, `actionDisabled`, `Icon`, `enableOverflow`, `forceOverlayWhenNoModal`, `preventCloseOnOutsideClick`, plus `size`.
  - `preventCloseOnOutsideClick` (`:79-83`) calls `e.preventDefault()` in `onPointerDownOutside`. That handler comes after `{...props}`, so a caller can't pass its own `onPointerDownOutside`.
  - There is no `hideClose` prop and no close "X" button in `DialogContent`. The only built-in close control is the separate `DialogClose` component (`:182-205`), which neither modal uses.
  - There is no escape-specific prop. Other Radix Content props such as `onEscapeKeyDown` and `onInteractOutside` do pass through via `...props`.
- Escape and outside clicks both close the dialog through Radix's `onOpenChange`:
  - Settings modal: dismissible, because its `onOpenChange` is the toggle.
  - Security modal: with `open={true}` and no `onOpenChange`, Radix can't close it, so only the Cancel button dismisses it.

- This path runs whenever `user` is absent (`:528-530`), which means every token refresh after sign-in.

- `two-factor-auth-view.tsx` passes the toggle `onOpenChange={() =&gt; setEnableModalOpen(!enableModalOpen)}`. Its `onEnable` (`:64-73`) calls `signOut({callbackUrl:"/auth/login"})` when `role === "INACTIVE_ADMIN`; otherwise it calls `utils.viewer.me.invalidate()`.

**Dialog internals:**

- `packages/ui/components/dialog/Dialog.tsx`:

  - `preventCloseOnOutsideClick` (`:79-83`) calls `e.preventDefault()` in `onPointerDownOutside`. That handler comes after `{...props}`, so a caller can't pass its own `onPointerDownOutside`.
  - There is no `hideClose` prop and no close "X" button in `DialogContent`. The only built-in close control is the separate `DialogClose` component (`:182-205`), which neither modal uses.
  - There is no escape-specific prop. Other Radix Content props such as `onEscapeKeyDown` and `onInteractOutside` do pass through via `...props`.
- Escape and outside clicks both close the dialog through Radix's `onOpenChange`:
  - Settings modal: dismissible, because its `onOpenChange` is the toggle.
  - Security modal: with `open={true}` and no `onOpenChange`, Radix can't close it, so only the Cancel button dismisses it.
